items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The speaker mentions hearing Herb Jeffreys sing on the radio with Duke Ellington's band, but does not describe any personal interaction or direct professional relationship with Jeffreys himself.

ctx.x: J.C. had a radio in his car and one night as we were coming from work, we caught a broadcast of Duke coming from somewhere in California. They were playing a number called "Flamingo" and a male singer was singing it. This fellow really had a wonderful

voice and Duke's band was sounding great as usual. But it was the singer that had really captured our attention. At the end of the number, the speaker announced that we just heard a new voice of the/Duke Ellington orchestra, Herb Jeffreys singing "Flamingo".

We always changed from our white uniforms after we finished a night and had a room in the hotel for that. And every two weeks we had them cleaned. A quick cleaner near the hotel would pick them up on a Monday and they would be ready for us when we returned Tuesday night. J.C., Al, myself were about the fastest changing members of the band, because sometimes we would arrive a little late dressed in our regular street clothes about 10 or 15 minutes before starting time.
